Messages.Author: midnight@inferno.com
Messages.Body:
Question about Culmatative Master Cards (Ie Protracted Investment etc)
If you have Anson in play and can play two master cards per turn, could
you take one blood off of say two Protracted Investments?
Also if Anson is in play and you use a Master Out of Turn it states in
the Rules you lose your master phase?  So I take it that means you can
not play your second Master card when your turn comes around, seeing as
you lose the whole Phase for using a Master out of Turn?
Midnight aka Steve Sharrard

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
<midnight@inferno.com> wrote:
>If you have Anson in play and can play two master cards per turn, could
>you take one blood off of say two Protracted Investments?

Yes.  You spend a master action, not your entire master phase, to take a
counter off an investment.

>Also if Anson is in play and you use a Master Out of Turn it states in
>the Rules you lose your master phase?  So I take it that means you can
>not play your second Master card when your turn comes around, seeing as
>you lose the whole Phase for using a Master out of Turn?

Right.

>

>
>So would this mean that things like Blood Doll (i.e. things that happen
>during your Master phase but are totally unrelated to playing Master cards)
>wouldn't be usable the turn after you play an out-of-turn Master card?
>
	Yep. You lose your master phase and so therefore lose the 
opportunity to transfer blood. (Side Note: Even if you do have the master 
phase and happen to able to perform more than one master action, you'd 
still only be able to pull one blood from the blood doll or give one, 
same thing.)
